title: Chemical properties of matter
competency: Identify chemical properties and distinguish them from physical properties.

keywords.def: Describes how a substance changes, or resists change, to form a new substance.
The ability of a substance to burn.
How a substance reacts with other substances.

en.text: A chemical property describes how a substance changes, or resists change, to form a new substance. We cannot find it just by looking or touching. Flammability and reactivity are chemical properties. Iron rusting in moist air shows a chemical property of iron.

screens.title: Will it burn?
screens.ask: Paper burns but a stone does not. Can you tell this just by looking at them?
opts: No, you must try to change them
screens.after: You cannot see flammability. You find it only when the substance changes (or does not). That is a chemical property.
screens.best: No, you must try to change them

screens.title: 2.2.2 Chemical properties of matter
paras: A chemical property describes how a substance undergoes or resists change to form a new substance.
It cannot be found just by viewing or touching the substance.
Flammability is one chemical property. Reactivity is another.

screens.title: Table 2.2 Physical and chemical properties
table: Describe how a substance changes to form a new one
Cannot be seen just by looking or touching
Internal structure must be affected to test it
Colour, density, volume, melting point, boiling point, conductivity

screens.title: Chemical properties you can test
screens.ask: Tap each one. How do we find it?
items: How easily a substance burns. Paper and plastic burn; a stone does not. Burning forms new substances.
How a substance reacts with others. Iron rusts in moist air. Nickel dissolves in acid.
Silver shows no reaction in hydrochloric acid. Resisting change is also a chemical property.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Describes how a substance changes, or resists change, to form a new substance.
The ability of a substance to burn.
How a substance reacts with other substances.

screens.text: Chemical property: which one is a chemical property?
screens.why:
Colour, density and melting point are found without change: physical.
Flammability is about burning.
Burning forms new substances such as ash, smoke and gases.
So "plastic is flammable" is the chemical property.
screens.clue: Which one is about forming something new?

items: Mercury is liquid at room temperature
Nickel dissolves in acid to give a green solution
Silver shows no reaction in hydrochloric acid
screens.why:
Ask: does it describe forming a new substance, or resisting that?
Rusting and nickel dissolving in acid form new substances: chemical.
Silver not reacting with acid is resisting change: also chemical.
State, colour and density are seen without change: physical.
screens.clue: Does a new substance form, or could it?
screens.text: Sort each statement: physical property or chemical property?
True or false: a chemical property can be found just by looking at a substance.
screens.why:
Looking shows physical properties, like colour.
To find a chemical property you must try to change the substance.
For flammability you must try to burn it.
So the statement is false.

screens.text: "Silver shows no sign of reaction in hydrochloric acid." Why is this a CHEMICAL property, even though nothing happens?
opts: It describes how silver resists change
screens.ans: It describes how silver resists change
screens.why:
The definition: how a substance undergoes OR resists change.
Silver is tested with acid, and it resists change.
This low reactivity is a chemical property.
"Nothing happening is always physical" is the trap: here it is the result of a chemical test.
screens.clue: Read the definition carefully: "undergoes or resists".

items.title: 1. Physical or chemical? (a–e)
items: a. Iron rusts in moist air
b. Mercury is a liquid at room temperature
c. Nickel dissolves in acid to give a green solution
items.why:
a. Rusting forms rust, a new substance: chemical.
b. Being liquid is a state: physical.
c. Dissolving in acid to give a green solution is a reaction: chemical.
d. A melting point and e. a colour are found without change: physical.
items.text: Exercise 2.5 Q1: sort each statement (a–e) as a physical or a chemical property.

items.title: 1. Physical or chemical? (f–j)
items: f. Titanium can be drawn into thin wires
g. Inhaled beryllium dust causes lung disease
h. Silver shows no reaction in hydrochloric acid
i. Lead is denser than aluminium
items.why:
f. Being drawn into wires changes only the shape: physical.
g. Beryllium dust reacts with body tissue: chemical.
h. Silver resisting acid is about reactivity: chemical.
i. Density is physical. j. Flammability is chemical.
items.text: Exercise 2.5 Q1: sort each statement (f–j) as a physical or a chemical property.

items.title: 2. Intensive or extensive?
items.why:
Imagine twice as much sample.
Length, mass and volume double: extensive.
Boiling point, colour, density and melting point stay the same: intensive.
items.text: Exercise 2.5 Q2: sort each property as intensive or extensive.

items.title: 3. Sense organs or measurable?
items.why:
Odour, taste and colour are sensed by the nose, tongue and eyes.
Density needs a balance and a cylinder; melting point needs a thermometer.
Conductivity needs a circuit.
So density, melting point and conductivity are measurable.
items.text: Exercise 2.5 Q3: sort each property: detected by sense organs, or measurable?

test.text: Chemical property: which one of these is a chemical property?
test.why:
Colour, density and boiling point are found without changing the substance: physical.
Flammability is found by trying to burn it.
Burning forms new substances.
Answer: flammability.

test.text: True or false: reactivity between two substances is a chemical property.
test.why:
Reactivity tells how a substance reacts with others.
Reacting forms new substances.
The book names reactivity as a chemical property.
So the statement is true.

test.text: Physical or chemical: "Iron metal rusts in moist air" describes a …
test.why:
Iron rusting forms rust, a new substance.
A property about changing into a new substance is chemical.
Answer: chemical property.

test.text: Chemical properties: which statement is true of chemical properties?
opts: They are easily seen by looking
They describe how a substance forms new substances
They are the same as colour
test.ans: They describe how a substance forms new substances
test.why:
Table 2.2: chemical properties describe how a substance changes to form new ones.
They cannot be seen just by looking, so the first option is wrong.
Colour is a physical property.
Answer: they describe how a substance forms new substances.

items: Iron is attracted by a magnet
test.why:
Charcoal burning forms ash and gases: chemical.
Magnesium reacting with acid forms new substances: chemical.
Gold's yellow colour is seen without change: physical.
Being pulled by a magnet does not change iron: physical.
test.text: Sort each statement: physical or chemical property?
